paragraphs.text: Drug companies pooled private protein data to improve an AI model
paragraphs.exact: Drug companies pooled private protein data to improve an AI model

paragraphs.text: Nature reports that five drug companies used 20,167 private protein structures to fine-tune a research AI model based on OpenFold3. On a held-out test, the reported model predicted more protein–molecule structures accurately than comparable models trained on public data alone. This is a research-model comparison, not an announcement of a new drug.
paragraphs.exact: Nature reports that five drug companies used 20,167 private protein structures to fine-tune a research AI model based on OpenFold3. On a held-out test, the reported model predicted more protein–molecule structures accurately than comparable models trained on public data alone. This is a research-model comparison, not an announcement of a new drug.

paragraphs.text: A protein model is an AI system that predicts how proteins and other molecules might fit together. A held-out test uses examples kept separate from training. The report says the extra data helped on that test, but the model is not public and the described study has not been peer reviewed.
